Happiness can arise when something wanted or unexpectedly good happens, a goal is achieved, connection is felt, or a pleasant experience is noticed.

## Words describing happiness

Amusement, bliss, cheerfulness, contentment, delight, eagerness, elation, enjoyment, enthusiasm, excitement, exhilaration, gladness, glee, hope, joy, optimism, pleasure, pride, relief, satisfaction, triumph, and zest.

## Prompting events and interpretations

Events include welcome surprises, getting what you want, success, esteem, affection, acceptance, belonging, pleasurable sensations, or feared outcomes not occurring. The source emphasizes interpreting joyful events as they are, without adding or subtracting.

## Body changes, expressions, and action urges

You may feel energetic, calm, warm, open, expansive, or ready to laugh. Actions can include smiling, sharing, connecting, hugging, moving, speaking enthusiastically, and continuing the activity.

## Aftereffects

Friendliness, kindness, a positive outlook, confidence, remembered joy, and expectation of future joy may increase.

## When happiness fits the facts

Happiness may fit when a wanted or unexpectedly good event occurs, a goal is achieved, or a pleasant connection or sensation is present. There is no standard Handout 11 Opposite Action page for happiness in this source set.

## Acting on the urge and Checking the Facts

When safe and effective, participate fully, share without pressure, and notice the pleasant experience. If intensity creates a problem, use Wise Mind and Check the Facts rather than treating happiness itself as wrong.
